question: How did the rule on NPA recognition for loans under a DLG change?
expected_answer: The old Digital Lending Directions made the lender responsible for NPA recognition regardless of DLG cover. In the NBFC Credit Facilities Directions this paragraph was substituted with effect from 13 February 2026; it now refers asset classification and provisioning to the NBFC IRACP Directions.
key_facts: Earlier: the lender was responsible for NPA recognition regardless of DLG cover | The paragraph was substituted with effect from 13 February 2026 | Now: asset classification and provisioning follow the NBFC IRACP Directions
system_answer:
Earlier: recognition of individual loan assets in the portfolio as NPA and consequent provisioning was the responsibility of the RE as per the extant asset classification and provisioning norms irrespective of any DLG cover available at the portfolio level; the amount of DLG invoked was not to be set off against the underlying individual loans; recovery, if any, could be shared with the DLG provider; and DLG amount once invoked was not to be reinstated, including through loan recovery. [S6]

Now: asset classification of individual loan assets and consequent provisioning requirement shall be in terms of the Reserve Bank of India (Non-Banking Financial Companies - Income Recognition, Asset Classification and Provisioning) Directions, 2025; the amount of DLG invoked shall not be set off against the underlying individual loans; recovery, if any, from the loans on which DLG has been invoked and realised, can be shared with the DLG provider in terms of the contractual arrangement; and DLG amount once invoked shall not be reinstated, including through loan recovery. [S1]
cited: S6 digital_lending_directions_2025.pdf para 24 p17-18 || S1 nbfc_credit_facilities_2025.pdf para 25 p26
my_notes: [graded by Claude (AI), not a human] earlier and now present; missing 'substituted w.e.f. 13 Feb 2026'
